blocks.content: Buffer stock is maintained by the government to ensure food security during lean seasons and stabilize market prices.

rows: Meets monthly distribution requirements of PDS and welfare schemes
Maintained for unforeseen emergencies, natural disasters, and crop failures
Drawn only during critical supply disruptions or severe price spikes
Calculated based on quarterly scheme demand and off-take projections
Fixed minimum quantity prescribed by CCEA over operational needs

items: CCEA (Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs) approves the minimum buffer stock norms, not the Ministry of Finance or RBI.
Food Corporation of India (FCI) was established under the Food Corporation Act, 1964 to execute procurement and buffer management.
Exams frequently ask to distinguish between Operational Stock (for monthly PDS off-take) and Strategic Reserve (for national calamities).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Buffer stock is the reserve of foodgrains maintained by the Food Corporation of India (FCI) on behalf of the Government.
Buffer stocking norms are fixed and periodically revised by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA).
The total stock comprises two components: Operational Stock for regular PDS supply and Strategic Reserve for unforeseen emergencies.
Minimum buffer norms are defined for four specific dates across the year: April 1, July 1, October 1, and January 1.
The policy helps stabilize market prices through the Open Market Sale Scheme (OMSS) and ensures national food security.
